text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended somewhat higher in the afternoon after trading in a tight range throughout the day. By the close, May was $1.00 stronger at $311.00 per tonne, the day's high, while August was 20 cents firmer at $308.00. Trading was dominated by cross and switch trade in a market preparing for the expiry of the spot May contract on April 15, traders said. Raw sugar futures in New York settled firmer but off the highs, having failed to trigger stops resting about 11.10 cents basis May, floor sources said.

The spot month is expected to remain close to 11.00 cents through May options expiry April 11, since open interest in the May 11.00 calls remains high at 7,216 lots as of Monday's close. The spot month closed at 11.04, up 0.04, having ranged from 11.08 to 11.00 cents. The back months closed 0.04 firmer to 0.01 lower.

CHINA - Sugar imports in February 1997 amounted to 29,258 tonnes, raw value, up from the January figure of 7,687 tonnes and also above the February 1996 volume of 2,619 tonnes. Cumulative imports so far in the 1996/97 (September/February) campaign reached 458,613 tonnes, sharply down from last year's 1.169 mn tonnes. Total imports in 1995/96 amounted to 1.944 mn tonnes against 2.907 mn tonnes in 1994/95. Major countries of origin in September/February 1996/97 were Australia with 253,739 tonnes raws against 326,995 tonnes, Cuba with 132,590 tonnes, down from 168,953 tonnes and Thailand with 29,382 tonnes compared to 236,453 tonnes. The largest white sugar supplier in September/February 1996/97 was South Korea with 19,490 tonnes compared to 16,718 tonnes. Sugar exports in February 1997 reached 15,163 tonnes, down from 65,114 tonnes in February 1996. PORTUGAL - Sugar imports in December 1996 reached 31,440 tonnes, raw value, up from 25,878 tonnes imported in December 1995. This brought cumulative imports in calendar year 1996 up to 310,625 tonnes compared to 312,542 tonnes in 1995. Major countries of origin in calendar year 1996 were Mauritius with 71,082 tonnes raws against 18,119 tonnes, Swaziland with 57,013 tonnes, up from 45,362 tonnes and Zimbabwe with 33,747 tonnes compared to 36,169 tonnes. Sugar exports in December 1996 reached 962 tonnes which brought total exports in 1996 up to 14,580 tonnes compared to 15,432 tonnes in 1995. The major country of destination in 1996 was Spain with 9,053 tonnes whites against 8,216 tonnes in 1995.
